title: SOURCE_TARGETS retired: BRIE subtask SQL uses newly created glue sessions, not the user statement session

analysis: BRIE is a user-visible BACKUP/RESTORE executor, so it initially looks like a promising internal-SQL state-ingress target
BRIEExec.Next creates tidbGlue with se=e.Ctx(), but task.RunBackup/task.RunRestore call into glue-created sessions for BR subtask SQL
tidbGlue.CreateSession calls CreateSession(gs.se), which is wired to session.CreateSession(ctx.GetStore()) and therefore creates a fresh session from the store
tidbGlue.UseOneShotSession also creates a new session with CreateSession(gs.se), defers CloseSession, and passes that one-shot session into BR task callbacks
tidbGlueSession.Execute and ExecuteInternal run SQL through gs.se, but that gs.se is the new glue/one-shot session, not the user statement session holding pending TxnReadTS or SnapshotInfoschema
The candidate is still useful as a selector negative sample: user-visible statement wrapper is not enough; the proof obligation needs state-carrier ownership, not only entrypoint ownership
source_anchors: pkg/executor/brie.go:249 buildBRIE constructs BRIEExec from the user statement
pkg/executor/brie.go:579-629 BRIEExec.Next registers the task and runs task.RunBackup/task.RunRestore through tidbGlue
pkg/executor/brie.go:704-709 tidbGlue.CreateSession creates a fresh session for glue.Session
pkg/executor/brie.go:748-760 tidbGlue.UseOneShotSession creates and closes a fresh one-shot session
pkg/executor/brie.go:768-786 tidbGlueSession.Execute/ExecuteInternal run internal SQL on gs.se
pkg/session/session.go:4017-4023 session.CreateSession creates a new session environment from the store
payload.why_not_execute: A RED for pending TxnReadTS consumption would require assuming BRIE subtask SQL reuses the user statement session. The source chain proves it does not; executing this target would mainly validate a false harness assumption.
payload.method_lesson: Split ownership into statement-entry ownership and state-carrier ownership. Only the latter justifies running the pending one-shot-state oracle.
payload.next_step: teach the source-target generator to down-rank or retire paths where the internal SQL is behind CreateSession/UseOneShotSession before scheduling cluster validation
